data.title: Trump Administration Hit With Lawsuit Over Giving Feds Access to Millions of Welfare Recipients’ Social Security Numbers: 'Gross Breach of Personal Privacy'
data.description:
More than 20 states and Washington, D.C., sued the Trump administration on Monday to block a policy that could give federal authorities access to Social Security numbers, immigration status and other personal information belonging to millions of welfare recipients.

Policy Expands Federal Access To TANF Data

The Federal Register notice says the government wants to confirm state compliance through audits, fraud investigations and monitoring. It adds Social Security numbers as searchable identifiers and allows ACF to use verification information from the Department of Homeland Security and Social Security Administration.

Benzinga reached out to the White House for comment but did not receive an immediate response.

States Call Plan A Sweeping Privacy Breach

The states argue that Congress assigned TANF eligibility verification to state governments and never authorized a sweeping federal data-sharing system. Their complaint calls ACF’s position an "extravagant" claim of authority and a "gross breach of personal privacy."

"Instead of helping families struggling with the rising cost of living, this administration is trying to turn antipoverty programs against the people they’re supposed to serve," New York Attorney General Letitia James said.

TANF distributes more than $16 billion annually to states, territories and tribal governments for cash assistance, job training, childcare, housing and other support for low-income families with children. The states warn that sharing records with immigration authorities could discourage legally eligible families from seeking help.

Coalition Seeks Court Intervention Before Deadline

Reuters reported that civil-rights and privacy groups filed a separate lawsuit in Brooklyn alleging Privacy Act violations.

The coalition says the policy violates the Administrative Procedure Act, federal privacy laws and the Constitution. It wants a judge to block the rule before Aug. 11, while the administration maintains stronger oversight will ensure states follow TANF rules.

data.title: Fresh Off Nasdaq Debut, Bending Spoons Lands Airtable in $2.25 Billion Takeover
data.description:
The deal values Airtable at an enterprise value of $1.285 billion. Including the company’s net cash and cash equivalents, the implied equity value is about $2.25 billion.

The transaction is expected to close later this year, subject to regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions.

Bending Spoons Makes First Acquisition Since Nasdaq Debut

The acquisition marks Bending Spoons’ first deal since its Nasdaq listing on July 1, 2026. It also adds Airtable to the company’s expanding software portfolio, following its acquisitions of AOL in January and Eventbrite in March.

Under the agreement, Bending Spoons will acquire all outstanding Airtable shares. Both companies will continue operating independently until the transaction closes.

Airtable Growth And AI Focus

Bending Spoons CEO and co-founder Luca Ferrari said Airtable has built a strong position in workflow management and collaborative software. He noted that Airtable’s annual recurring revenue grew more than 20% year over year to about $480 million as of June 2026.

Ferrari said Bending Spoons plans to invest in the platform over the long term, with a focus on expanding product capabilities and accelerating innovation.

Airtable co-founder and CEO Howie Liu said the partnership will provide the resources needed to advance the company’s vision of building an AI-native platform. He added that Airtable now serves more than 500,000 organizations, including 80% of the Fortune 100.

Willkie Farr & Gallagher is acting as legal counsel to Bending Spoons, while Goldman Sachs Bank Europe and J.P. Morgan are serving as financial advisors. Latham & Watkins is advising Airtable, with AXOM Partners acting as its financial advisor.

Bending Spoons Price Action

BSP Price Action: Bending Spoons shares were trading higher by 2.84% at $37.25 during premarket trading on Tuesday, according to Benzinga Pro data.

data.title: Earnings Volatility Watch: SanDisk and Nine Other Stocks Could Swing Up To 17.5% This Week
data.description:
Screening Benzinga Pro data for U.S.-listed companies worth more than $50 billion, these are the 10 largest implied movers of the week.

Which Stocks Could Swing The Most This Week?

The implied move is the percentage change that options markets expect a stock to make over a specific period, in this case around an earnings announcement, based on current option prices.

10. Constellation Energy: 9.00% Implied Move

The nuclear power producer reports Aug. 6 before the open. Analyst consensus calls for $7.95 billion in revenue and earnings at $2.42 per share.

Watch new power purchase agreements with data center customers, nuclear output and the Calpine integration.

Constellation Energy Corp. (NASDAQ:CEG) heads into the print down 25.5% for 2026.

9. Petrobras: 9.58% Implied Move

The Brazilian oil major reports Aug. 6 after the close. Watch production volumes, refining margins with Brent near $90 and the size of the next dividend declaration.

Petróleo Brasileiro S.A. (NYSE:PBR) has climbed 51.4% since January.

8. Novo Nordisk: 9.65% Implied Move

The GLP-1 drugmaker reports Aug. 5 before the open. Analysts model $11.35 billion in revenue and earnings of 81 cents per share.

Wegovy and Ozempic prescription trends, supply and competition from Eli Lilly are the swing factors.

Novo Nordisk A/S (NYSE:NVO) is off 7.8% on the year.

7. DoorDash: 10.12% Implied Move

The food delivery platform reports Aug. 5 after the close. Consensus sits at $4.33 billion in revenue and earnings of 45 cents per share.

Total orders, gross order value and the pace of grocery and new-vertical growth are what matters.

DoorDash Inc. (NASDAQ:DASH) has slipped 13.5% in 2026.

6. Shopify: 12.47% Implied Move

The e-commerce platform reports Aug. 6 before the open. Analysts expect $3.44 billion in revenue and earnings of 40 cents per share.

Gross merchandise volume, take rate and operating margin drive the reaction.

Shopify Inc. (NYSE:SHOP) sits 26.5% lower year to date.

5. Cloudflare: 12.68% Implied Move

The connectivity and security company reports Aug. 6 after the close. Analyst consensus calls for $665.50 million in revenue and earnings of 27 cents per share.

Large-customer additions, net revenue retention and traction in AI inference products are the levers.

Cloudflare Inc. (NYSE:NET) has gained 42.4% this year.

4. Datadog: 12.88% Implied Move

The observability software firm reports Aug. 6 before the open. Analysts model $1.08 billion in revenue and earnings of 59 cents per share.

Net revenue retention, large-customer growth and AI-native customer contribution are the tell.

Datadog Inc. (NASDAQ:DDOG) has nearly doubled in 2026, up 99.9%.

3. AppLovin: 12.96% Implied Move

The mobile advertising company reports Aug. 5 after the close. Consensus sits at $1.94 billion in revenue and earnings at $3.72 per share.

Advertising engine revenue, the e-commerce ad rollout and EBITDA margin drive the move.

AppLovin Corp. (NASDAQ:APP) has lost 42.1% year to date, the worst performer on this list.

2. Western Digital: 13.39% Implied Move

The hard drive maker reports Aug. 5 after the close. Analysts expect $3.69 billion in revenue and earnings at $3.29 per share.

Nearline drive demand from data centers, exabyte shipments and pricing set the tone for the standalone HDD business.

Western Digital Corp. (NASDAQ:WDC) has more than tripled, up 222.2% for the year.

1. SanDisk: 17.47% Implied Move

The memory chip maker reports Aug. 5 after the close. Analysts model $8.39 billion in revenue and earnings at $34.45 per share.

NAND pricing, enterprise SSD demand for AI and gross margin are what the market is pricing.

Up 423.2% in 2026, SanDisk Corp. (NASDAQ:SNDK) towers over the rest of this group.
